about: The collect among the prayers of Leo XIII, said after the Salve Regína and its versicle; its first words are Psalm 45:2, the psalm's nominative turned into a vocative. The prayers after low Mass were instituted by Pius IX in 1859 for the Papal States; Leo XIII extended them to the whole Church in 1884, and the text printed here is his rewriting of 1886 — that is when the petitions for the freedom of the Church and the conversion of sinners came in. When the Lateran treaties settled the Roman Question in 1929, Pius XI directed the year after that these prayers be offered for Russia. It is built like a Roman collect — one sentence in which everything leads to the imperative — except that the imperatives here are two: look upon, and hear. It closes with “through the same Christ”, because the prayer is addressed to the Father and the Son has been named in it only obliquely, in the title Mother of God.

s02.translation: O God, our refuge and our strength, look with favour upon the people crying out to Thee;

s03.translation: and by the intercession of the glorious and immaculate Virgin Mary, Mother of God,

s04.translation: with blessed Joseph her Spouse, and Thy blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the Saints,

s05.translation: the prayers we pour out for the conversion of sinners, for the freedom and exaltation of holy Mother Church,

s07.translation: Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

w001.function: A subjunctive urging rather than stating: not “we are praying” but a call to pray together.

w002.function: Vocative, which for this noun is the nominative form. The collect opens by naming the one it speaks to.

w003.function: In apposition to “Deus” (w002): God named by what he is to those asking. The noun names not the flight itself but the place fled to — as in the invocation “Refuge of sinners”.

w006.function: The second half of the apposition; “nostrum” (w004) covers both.

w007.function: Accusative, the object of “réspice” (w012), which will not arrive until the end of the line.

w010.function: A participle in the accusative agreeing with “pópulum” (w007): the people as they are crying.

w011.function: An adjective where English wants an adverb: Latin says the one who looks is favourable, not that he looks favourably.

w012.function: The first of the sentence's two imperatives; the second, “exáudi” (w053), closes it forty words later.

w014.function: The head of an ablative absolute: a construction standing outside the sentence's grammar and giving the circumstance. With “Vírgine” (w018) it means: the Virgin interceding.

w018.function: The noun of the ablative absolute; both adjectives before it agree with it.

w020.function: In apposition to “Vírgine” (w018), in the same case.

w022.function: A new phrase, outside the ablative absolute now: it joins the saints to the Virgin's intercession.

w024.function: An indeclinable name: ablative here, though the form never changes. Latin took it in twice — as the unchanging Ioseph and as the declined Iosephus — and one witness prints Josepho in this place.

w025.function: The genitive of the demonstrative, pointing back to Mary in the line before.

w036.function: An adjective used as a noun: holy people.

w037.function: A relative pronoun, feminine accusative plural. It stands eleven words before its own noun — “preces” (w048) — which is ordinary Latin and has to be read backwards.

w047.function: Genitive: the freedom and the exaltation belong to the Church, named here as a holy Mother.

w048.function: The noun “quas” (w037) was waiting for, and the object of “exáudi” (w053).

w049.function: Literally, we pour out. First person plural — the whole people speaking, not the priest alone.

w052.function: Adjectives again where English wants adverbs, as with “propítius” (w011) in the opening line.

w053.function: The second imperative; its object is “preces” (w048), five words back — waited for since “quas” (w037).

w055.function: The formula “per eúndem” is used when the Son has already been named in the prayer. Here he is named only obliquely, in the title “Genetríce” (w020), Mother of God.
